world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Leidenfrost, Csaba Tokpa. 2007. Discourse Studies in Bakwé: preliminary notes on Bakwé discourse grammar (234pp). Only substantial description listed; not online. No phonology/grammar of Bakwé found; webonary Bakwé dictionary returned 403.

new_statements.quote: Le bakwé est une langue musicale, c'est-à-dire que les mots ne se distinguent pas seulement par les lettres, mais aussi par leur mélodie. La hauteur musicale avec laquelle on prononce les mots est appelée le ton du mot. En bakwé, il y a trois niveaux de tons, qu'on appelle haut, moyen et bas. [...] Si le mot est plus long, il consiste en deux, trois, quatre et même plus de syllabes, dont chacune porte au moins un ton. Cependant, il suffit de marquer le ton de la première syllabe du mot pour qu'un locuteur bakwé puisse lire le mot correctement.
new_statements.translation: Bakwé is a musical language, that is, words are distinguished not only by their letters but also by their melody. The musical pitch with which words are pronounced is called the tone of the word. In Bakwé there are three tone levels, called high, mid and low. [...] If the word is longer, it consists of two, three, four or even more syllables, each of which carries at least one tone. However, it suffices to mark the tone of the first syllable of the word for a Bakwé speaker to read the word correctly.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bakwé is a register-tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low) plus contour tones written with doubled/tripled vowels; every syllable bears a tone and nouns have lexical tone melodies (level H, level M, rising L-M, L-H, M-H, L-H-M). No source opened says anything about word stress or accent, so no stress rule can be stated; the three-level analysis is independently confirmed by Vogler 2017, p. 33 ('Le bakwé est une langue à trois niveaux de registres').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone notes: proper names may be written without tone marks; a word-final high tone 'belongs to the preceding vowel' (Syllabaire 2019, p. 9; Guide de prononciation).
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern the word (lexical tone of nouns and verbs, citation forms in a literacy primer); the tone-melody classes are given for simple nouns. The primer is a literacy/orthography guide by the Bakwé translation-literacy project (SIL-facilitated), not a linguistic phonology; it describes the dɛplɛɛ (Deple) dialect used for the orthography (dictionary and syllabaire are explicitly 'en dɛplɛɛ').
new_statements.identity_note: The C.T.A.B. materials describe the dɛplɛɛ (Deple) dialect of Bakwé (the dictionary and the 2019 syllabaire are explicitly 'en dɛplɛɛ'; a separate Cours-éclair exists for Nyragbi/Nigagba), spoken around Touadji II / Meagui; Ethnologue lists dialects Defa, Deple, Dafa, Nigagba, Nyinagbi, all under bakw1243 (no separate glottocodes).

sources.note: Nothing about stress/accent. Leçon 1 'Les tons' (p. 4): Bakwé is a 'langue musicale' with three tone levels (haut, moyen, bas), every syllable carries at least one tone, only the first syllable's tone is written; Leçon 9 (pp. 19-21) lists noun tone melodies (level H, level M; rising L-M, L-H, M-H, L-H-M). Only mention of 'accent' is orthographic (no accent on é).

sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog lists no grammar or phonology for Bakwé (only Leidenfrost 2007 as 'specific_feature', the 2006 dictionary, overviews and wordlists). OLAC/SIL list the C.T.A.B. literacy materials and Leidenfrost 2007 as language descriptions.

sources.note: p. 9 'LES TONS': high tone (apostrophe), mid (unmarked), low (hyphen); two or three identical vowels mark a contour ('ton modulé'); a word-final high tone belongs to the preceding vowel. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre. 2017. Contribution à la classification des langues kru (Niger-Congo). HAL hal-01574391v2. 74 pp.
sources.note: §3.56, p. 33: 'Le bakwé est une langue à trois niveaux de registres, mais il est vrai que ce type est dominant dans le secteur et concerne aussi le neyo et le godié.' §2.4 (p. 7): Kru tone systems have three or four registers. Nothing on stress; cites Leidenfrost 2007 as the recent Bakwé documentation (Touadji II).
